eventTypes.description: A Work Item has been dispatched to a Participant for execution.
Chapter 8 §18 — a commissioning attempt has begun; the SEU's Pending row now exists.

Chapter 8 §18/§9 — the shallow "Validate Request" gate passed (existence, authorisation, live Pack/Ontology references). No subscriber — Compose EBM is a manual transition; a human must click "Compose" on the Compose EBM page to begin it.
Chapter 8 §18 — commissioning failed, either at the shallow Validate Request gate or with unresolved conflicts during Compose EBM.

Chapter 8 §18/§10 — Compose EBM has begun. Currently unpublished: the manual "Compose"/"Apply & re-validate" routes (web/objectives.ts) don't emit it; only CompositionCompleted marks the real outcome.
Chapter 3 §15 — a new EBM has been persisted (status Composed), pending manual Validate Engineering Model review.

Chapter 3 §15/Chapter 8 §8 — a human has manually confirmed a composed EBM is still live (transitionEbm, targetState Validated). No subscriber — Activate is a separate, independently human-triggered transition; a human must click "Activate" on the SEU detail page to begin it.

Chapter 3 §15 — a later, execution-time recomposition producing a new EBM version off a Behaviour Conflict (owner: "we have not reached there yet"). Currently unpublished — this pass never produces a second EBM version for the same SEU.

Chapter 3 §15 — a human manually confirmed the Validated EBM should take effect (transitionEbm, targetState Active). CR-102: transitionEbm itself only updates status and publishes this event; ebmActivatedHandler (async subscriber) runs finalizeCommissioning off it — failure is signaled via seus.lifecycle_state = Failed + CommissionFailed, not a caller return.
Chapter 8 §18 — Compose EBM finished with zero composition conflicts (either on the first pass, or after a human resolved every conflict); the ebms row may now be created.
Chapter 3 §15 — a Validate attempt found this EBM's own Template/Profile/composed Packs are no longer all live (checkEbmLiveness); status set to Retired instead of Validated.

Chapter 2/8 — seus.lifecycle_state set to Configured. Published by finalizeCommissioning (CR-102: called from ebmActivatedHandler, off EBMActivated), deliberately ahead of SEUCommissioned (owner: "let us stick to the order I gave").
Chapter 2/8 — seus.lifecycle_state set to Commissioned. Published by finalizeCommissioning, on the way to Activated.

Chapter 2/8 — seus.lifecycle_state set to Activated. Published by finalizeCommissioning as its own last statement, right after Create Engineering Assets (CR-107: moved ahead of this hop). SEU|Activated|Operational is now trigger: "governed" — executionEngineKickoff subscribes to this and attempts that hop (Transition Definition, Policy, apply + publish), the Execution Engine's own first real reactive decision (Ch.31 §9).

Chapter 2/8 — seus.lifecycle_state set to Operational, the final hop. Published by attemptSeuCommenceWork (executionEngineKickoff.ts / commissioning.ts) once the SEU-scoped commence-work Policy passes. CR-104's own 'kickoff of the first Deliverable' question: deliverableKickoffHandler subscribes to this and attempts every Deliverable's own next Transition Definition via transitionDeliverable, self-filtered by that call's own governance (dependency readiness first).

Chapter 23 §9 — an Obligation moved to a new lifecycle state (payload: fromState/toState). Published by transitionObligation for every hop, not just the terminal ones. CR-107 (formerly CR-106 Option C's obligationResolved, folded in): executionEngineKickoff subscribes to this and, when toState is Verified/Closed/Archived, the Obligation is related to a SEU, and it carries a recorded blocked_from_state/blocked_to_state, re-attempts the SEU commence-work hop it was blocking.
Ch.31 §10/§15 — executionEngine.execute() persisted a Command. commandGeneratedHandler (async subscriber) runs Work Item generation off it; execute() itself publishes and returns, nothing after.
Ch.32 — workItemGenerator.generate() persisted a Work Item. workItemGeneratedHandler (async subscriber) runs dispatchEngine.dispatch() off it; generate() itself publishes and returns, nothing after.

Chapter 9 — a Deliverable's governed transition completed (payload: fromState/toState). Published by completeWorkItem when a Participant reports `done`. deliverableKickoffHandler subscribes to this too (same handler as SEUOperational) so each completed hop re-scans the SEU's Deliverables and attempts whichever one this just unblocked — the succession mechanism, not just the first kickoff.

Ch.33 §14 — qualified candidates exist, none currently Available (transient). Published since the original dispatchEngine.ts, pre-dating this session, but never registered until now. Consumed by redispatchRequest, which publishes RedispatchRequested.

Ch.33 §14 — no producing Capability declared, or the eligible-Participant pool is empty. An Obligation + Action-Required Attention Item are raised and the Command is marked Failed. No direct consumer — retrying happens only once a human resolves the Obligation, via ObligationTransitioned.

Ch.33 §14 — the eligible pool has entries, but Dispatch Strategy filtering eliminates every candidate structurally. Same Obligation + Action-Required Attention Item + Command-Failed treatment as DispatchRejected, same no-direct-consumer reasoning.

Ch.33 §14 — DispatchDeferred's own consumer requesting a retry: qualified candidates exist but none are currently Available. Consumed by a retry handler that re-runs dispatchEngine.dispatch on the same Work Item.
Ch.33 §14 — a RedispatchRequested retry landed on a successful Participant assignment (published alongside ParticipantSelected/WorkItemDispatched, not instead of them).
